settings.heading: Is PCOS the same as PMOS?
settings.row_content: No — "PMOS" is a common misspelling. The correct name is PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome).

settings.heading: Can PCOS be cured?
settings.row_content: There is currently no cure, but symptoms can often be managed effectively through a combination of medical care and lifestyle habits.

settings.heading: Does everyone with PCOS have cysts on their ovaries?
settings.row_content: Not necessarily. Despite the name, some women diagnosed with PCOS don't have visible cysts, while others without PCOS may have them. Diagnosis is based on a combination of factors, not cysts alone.

settings.heading: Can you get pregnant with PCOS?
settings.row_content: Yes. While PCOS can make conception more challenging for some women, many go on to conceive — sometimes with medical support. Speak with your healthcare provider about your options.

settings.heading: Do supplements help with PCOS?
settings.row_content: Some ingredients have been studied for their role in supporting hormonal and metabolic health, but supplements should support, not replace, medical care and lifestyle changes.
